transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Patel (Redwood SE), Rajesh Kumar (NovaPay SRE), Aisha Malik (NovaPay ML Engineer), Tom Hernandez (NovaPay CTO)

Summary (auto): week 4 POC throughput sync, empiric results reviewed, tuning plan agreed, follow-ups assigned.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Rajesh: yeah rajesh here. we got a few infra folks around but mostly me and aisha today.
[00:09] Aisha: hi this is aisha, ml eng.
[00:12] Tom: tom here, ct o, will drop in for the first 10.
[00:15] Maya: great, luca from my side as se, we'll go through the latest throughput runs. we pushed the continuous batching patch and adjusted concurrency targets as discussed.
[00:25] Luca: yeah quick note - we changed two knobs: continuous batching enabled with max_batch_time set to 20ms, and we increased per-worker concurrency from 2 -> 5 for the 80-token average workload. also set a max_queue_ms of 50ms to cap tail latency.
[00:40] Rajesh: initial numbers looked promising in the lab, but our staging runs showed some tail latency spikes when traffic bursts hit.
[00:45] Maya: right, that was expected tradeoff. we saw throughput jump ~2.6x on average but p95 tail latency went from ~120ms to ~420ms under bursty QPS, mostly due to queueing and some large prompts.
[01:05] Aisha: i'm wondering about prompt length distribution - on real traffic we have a bimodal distribution, lots of short 40-90 tokens but then 10% long 400-600 token invoice-generation prompts. those long ones are causing KV cache misses and bigger batches that block the queue.
[01:25] Luca: yep that matches our tracing. the long prompts increase per-token compute and hold GPUs longer. continuous batching helps amortize kernel overhead for short prompts but mixes in long ones and increases latency.
[01:40] Maya: so proposal: two concurrent routing lanes. lane A for short prompts - aggressive batching, higher concurrency. lane B for long prompts - lower concurrency, smaller max_batch_size, and bypass queue to reduce head-of-line blocking.
[01:55] Tom: does that mean we need model sharding or separate pools? cost implications?
[02:02] Luca: you can do soft partitioning with request classifier at edge - route by estimated prompt length or intent. no need for separate model binaries, same model just different instance pools if you want hard isolation. that will have some cost but reduces tail latency.
[02:18] Rajesh: in staging we have a single pool right now. hard to add pools until procurement moves. want to try soft rules first.
[02:24] Maya: agreed. we can add routing rules in the gateway to detect length and route. also set per-lane concurrency targets; for short prompt lane target concurrency 8 per worker, long prompt lane 1-2.
[02:40] Aisha: what about KV cache warm-up? during the POC we saw performance ramp over first 10 minutes. can we pre-warm some prefixes for invoices?
[02:50] Luca: yes, prefix caching helps. we recommended a small warm-up job that primes the KV cache with common invoice templates and named entities. that reduced initial latency from ~900ms to ~320ms on our microbench.
[03:08] Rajesh: nice. do you have the warm-up script?
[03:11] Maya: we'll share it - action item.
[03:13] [03:13] Tom: slight crosstalk sorry - but i'm chiefly focused on SLOs. we need throughput targets but also a p95 goal under our 95th percentile request mix. what numbers are realistic?
[03:26] Luca: for the mixed workload with the two-lane approach we saw p95 ~260-300ms and throughput up ~2x vs baseline. if you go single pool with high concurrency you can push 2.5-3x but p95 jumps.
[03:40] Rajesh: our production target is p95 < 300ms for interactive payments flows and throughput >= 150 qps sustained. baseline on our infra was 55 qps.
[03:52] Maya: ok so two-lane approach seems to meet that. we should run a sustained 24h soak with that config and realistic trace to confirm autoscaling behaviour.
[04:02] Aisha: about autoscaling - we saw some oscillation with the default policy, scale up was fine but scale down sometimes too aggressive causing thrash.
[04:12] Luca: yeah tweak cooldown windows and use rate-based scaling on GPU pool. Redwood Dedicated offers reserve capacity + burst which helps prevent thrashing for critical windows.
[04:22] Tom: cost - any rough delta if we keep a small reserved pool?
[04:25] Maya: rough ballpark from POC numbers: dedicated reserved baseline increases fixed monthly cost but reduces per-token unit cost by ~15%. we'll send a simple model later.
[04:35] Rajesh: for now procurement wants to avoid a long-term commitment until we hit stability, so we try soft routing + 24h soak.
[04:42] Luca: cool. also we added a queuing param max_queue_ms (the max time a request can wait before being rejected or falling back). we set it to 50ms in the run, which bounded the tail but did show some 429 rejections under spikes.
[05:00] Maya: yes if rejections are unacceptable we can route to Hosted fallback model or lower concurrency. fallback is a graceful degradation you can enable.
[05:08] Rajesh: fallback to hosted isn't ideal due to data residency but might be ok for non-sensitive flows. need to document which routes can fallback.
[05:20] Aisha: one more note - our infer infra uses token-limit 2048 but we plan to move to 4096 soon. will batching heuristics need retuning?
[05:29] Luca: yep, longer context affects memory and batch packing; we'll re-run heuristics once you flip to 4k. we can give guidance beforehand.
[05:38] Tom: can you walk quickly through the lab numbers you shared in the deck?
[05:42] Maya: sure; slide 3 shows throughput vs concurrency for the 80-token baseline: concurrency 2 -> 5 doubled throughput from ~60 qps to 120 qps per worker, enabling continuous batching added another ~1.3x. solid numbers but p95 effects noted.
[06:00] Luca: slide 4 shows mixed workload with two-lane routing; throughput ~140 qps sustained with p95 ~270ms. trace sample included.
[06:12] Rajesh: the staging run uploaded last night - there's a spreadsheet link (we reference it) - but some of the runs show large variance around hour 3-4, any idea?
[06:20] Luca: likely warm-up pattern plus a traffic spike that hit long-prompt lane and queued short prompts behind it. logs show head-of-line blocking.
[06:30] Maya: mitigation: route by estimated compute cost rather than raw token length. classifier can look at prompt type (invoice vs small chat) to estimate. that reduces misclassification for few percent of requests.
[06:42] Aisha: classifier false-positive rate?
[06:44] Luca: we saw ~4% misclassifications in lab; mostly conservative - long prompts misrouted to short lane cause issues; we can add a secondary check using initial token count.
[06:56] Rajesh: sounds workable. i want to flag one constraint: our SSO flows cannot tolerate >1% 429 for auth flows. we need strict route exceptions.
[07:05] Maya: good call - we can pin auth endpoints to a dedicated small pool to guarantee no rejects.
[07:12] Tom: regarding security and compliance - can you re-share the SOC2 summary and audit log retention options?
[07:18] Maya: yes will attach the security pack (SOC2, ISO summaries) and options for audit log retention and KMS integration.
[07:25] Rajesh: on encryption, do we get a customer-managed KMS for the Dedicated option?
[07:29] Luca: yes, Redwood Private or Dedicated supports CMK via your cloud KMS or HSM. we documented per earlier slides.
[07:38] Aisha: ok, next on technical checklist: Luca will run a model-level trace to show where latency spends are (kernel vs queue vs IO).
[07:46] Luca: yep i'll produce a flamegraph and brief notes.
[07:49] Maya: action items recap: i'll send test config and warm-up script; luca will share traces and flamegraph; rajesh will kick off 24h soak; everyone reconvene after soak to review.
[08:05] Tom: sounds good. any risks we missed?
[08:08] Rajesh: procurement timeline - if the soak looks good we may discuss reserved capacity but that's 2-3 weeks out.
[08:15] Maya: ok, we'll provide cost estimates and a decision checklist to help procurement.
[08:20] Aisha: one last question - when you say continuous batching, is there a config we can tune in runtime? where is it exposed?
[08:27] Luca: it's exposed as max_batch_time, min_batch_size, batching_policy and also max_queue_ms. we will include the param reference in the config we share.
[08:36] Rajesh: perfect.
[08:38] Tom: i'm stepping out, thanks everyone.
[08:40] Maya: thanks tom. quick reminder: we'll aim to share artifacts by EOD tomorrow and Rajesh will start soak by Friday.
[08:50] Rajesh: yep starting Friday morning PST.
[08:53] Maya: great, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription contains small errors typical of automated transcript; speakers sometimes overlap. References: shared spreadsheet: https://redwood-internal.example.com/poc/nova-pay-throughput-results (internal link), warm-up script: attached in follow-up email.
